questions.question: Explain in your own words when you should use the quadratic formula instead of trying to factorise.
questions.expected_answer: You should use the quadratic formula when a quadratic equation cannot be easily factorised because its roots are irrational (involving surds), or when you cannot find integer factors that multiply to 'ac' and add to 'b'.

questions.question: What is the discriminant, and why is it useful to calculate it first?
questions.expected_answer: The discriminant is the expression b² - 4ac under the square root. It is useful because it tells you the nature of the roots before you calculate them (positive = 2 distinct real roots, zero = 1 repeated real root, negative = no real roots).
